title: Unsubscribe from Everything
setup: Goodboy locks the city ledger before the public vote. The resistance has one night to unlock essential services without deleting ownership claims, debts under dispute or medical access.
escalation: The five cats enter the server core through the service level discovered earlier. Byte partitions records, Ghost obtains physical access, Neon maintains power, Onyx shields workers and Trixie relinquishes the sole administrator key to a public multi-party process. Fetch tries to stop them as Barkington flees to a secure executive suite.
resolution: The city gains a working public essentials ledger, the immediate lockout ends and the concession vote removes Goodboy's monopoly. Food access and the season's coordinated service extortion are genuinely resolved. The cats and ordinary dogs celebrate together. Barkington retains a separate security contract and uses it to launch BARK cameras under a public-safety promise.
continuity: The finale pays off the main season conflict before introducing BARK surveillance. The victory remains real. BARK cameras record vehicle plates and visible movements across connected streets; they do not read minds or see everywhere. Cat and dog civilians both object. CARETAKER is not publicly revealed in this final tag; its activation moves to the Season 2 opening.
comedy: Their new public login finally works. The first citizen complaint is still about a missing salmon coupon.
ending_hook: During the final two minutes, installers raise BARK SECURITY cameras above the reopened market. A dog shopkeeper objects that nobody voted for them. The crew sees the same vehicle appear in linked camera records; a routine trip is now a searchable trail. A BARK lens turns toward Trixie and the dog shopkeeper standing together. Its red status light comes on. Cut to black.
status: Development draft — not scripted or recorded
